trust_decision.summary: The userland BPF interpreter trusts the filter program's unconditional-jump offsets. At the pinned commit it checks only that the BPF_JA target is in bounds, not that the program terminates: a self-jump or an unbounded backward-jump loop runs forever. The validator also accepts the self-jump (k == -1).

landing_point.why: The advisory title names "ja L" looping in pcap_offline_filter(), and pcap_offline_filter (pcap.c:4362-4368) calls straight into the BPF_JA case of pcapint_filter_with_aux_data.

fix_sites.entry_point: pcap_offline_filter() (pcap.c:4362), deprecated bpf_filter() (bpf_filter.c:630-635), and the per-packet userland filtering in capture modules after pcap_setfilter (e.g. savefile.c:688, pcap-linux.c:4281)
bpf_validate() (bpf_filter.c:638-641), pcapint_install_bpf_program() via pcap_setfilter (optimize.c:2966), rpcapd filter upload (rpcapd/daemon.c:2403)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Every execution route goes through the single interpreter pcapint_filter_with_aux_data (bpf_filter.c:99-469). bpf_image.c and optimize.c only print or optimise programs; they do not run them.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that the validator (bpf_filter.c:600) needs no change once the interpreter is bounded, or that bpf_filter() is deprecated and documented as unsafe (bpf_filter.c:625-628). Both are weak, because the interpreter fix covers every route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: "ip6 protochain" and "protochain" compile to legitimate backward BPF_JA jumps that loop once per IPv6 extension header. Rejecting all backward or negative jumps in the validator or interpreter would break these filters.

O6_input_shapes: BPF_JA with k == -1 (self-jump), rejected in both validator and interpreter
BPF_JA with another negative k forming a multi-instruction backward loop, bounded by MAX_BACKWARD_JUMPS (64) per packet in the interpreter

O7_producer.where: Filter programs come from the caller (struct bpf_program) or from gencode.c. pcap_offline_filter does not call the validator (pcap.c:4365-4368).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A wrapper-level iteration or retry around pcapint_filter, or a second copy of the interpreter for a capture module (e.g. an aux-data variant), that lacks the backward-jump budget.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pcapint_filter_with_aux_data already exists as a Linux-specific variant (pcap-linux.c:4281). A maintainer could plausibly have forked it instead of adding a parameter.

O9_family: CWE-835 infinite loop in a bytecode interpreter (unbounded backward jumps)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf/make or CMake, plus flex/bison for the filter grammar
O10_build.project_tests: testprogs/filtertest.c compiles and validates filters (testprogs/filtertest.c:338). The fix diff adds no tests for the interpreter.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject backward jumps, or only k == -1, in pcapint_validate_filter. pcap_offline_filter and bpf_filter never call the validator, and rejecting all backward jumps breaks protochain.

out_of_scope_notes: The four sibling CVEs just before this one (CVE-2026-6244, -31911, -31912, -0799) harden the same interpreter; the area is heavily revised and written up.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run).
single_site is flagged on substance: one interpreter function plus a one-line validator mirror in the same file, with no O2 or O8. Strictly the fix touches two functions.
Whether 64 backward jumps are always enough for legitimate protochain on packets with many extension headers was not checked.
